claim: Three follow-ups to ev-20261011-chain-lab. (1) The RawAccel engine's tracking error is not an artefact of the assumed USB jitter: with ZERO jitter it is still 2.4x (BO6) to 9.5x (Psylocke) Cadence Lock's, from the integer count lattice alone, and it grows steeply with jitter (Psylocke 0.12 deg at 0% -> 4.6 deg at +/-40%) while Cadence Lock stays at the one-count floor (~0.012 deg) at every jitter. Across the roster Cadence Lock tracks 4-9x steadier. (2) A finer count lattice for the RawAccel engine (OTD px/mm xN, RawAccel multiplier /N, same sens and physics) is REJECTED: under jitter it barely helps (BO6 0.049 -> 0.044 deg) and from x2 VMulti splits reports below the curve's cap, making fast flicks 2.5-7 deg wrong. (3) The VMulti split hazard: at 90 px/mm VMulti splits every report above 508 mm/s; two wildcard cards (owwx Guardrail, hdwx Cannonade) have curves that still change above that, and the RawAccel engine misprices their fast flicks by 7-8 deg per 100 ms (owwx delivers ~18% long). A closed-form rule (BuildState.SplitHazardMmS) flags exactly those two of 86 cards, in agreement with the chain lab on every card; Cadence Lock is immune (0.006 deg).
method: ChainLab (see ev-20261011-chain-lab): --chain-lab --jitter N (0-40% of an interval), --lattice-lab (N = 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4), --split-hazard; selftest pins the rule against the chain lab for all 86 cards.

consequence: The window shows each card's real-chain tracking error on both engines (Engine tab). owwx and hdwx get the CADENCE chip and the one-click 'Apply this on Cadence Lock' with the reason; no card's curve or copy changed. Defaults unchanged: the RawAccel engine stays the default because the field-proven BO6 baseline was rated on it; Cadence Lock's field verdict is the open question this evidence sharpens.
fieldVerdict: pending - A/B Cadence Lock vs the RawAccel engine on your main card (Ctrl+Tab), and on owwx/hdwx if you play them
